summary:
FOUR ITEMS, FOUR REFUSALS LANDED, ALL FOUR RUN THROUGH THE REAL COMPOSITION ROOT.

WHAT WAS DONE. Two refusals, in the two entry points that are the first read INSIDE the package.
  1. src/memory/api.py::open_store now refuses MEM_QUOTA < 1 and MEM_OWNERS < 1 by name, at the top of
     the body, before the wires are narrowed and before Store.__init__ allocates anything.
  2. src/data/api.py::data_plan now refuses DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX and DATA_EXPOSURE_SKEW at nan and at
     +inf by name, at the top of the body, before the phase schedule is parsed.
Both declaration files record what 0 (and what nan/inf) means for the levers concerned, beside the
declaration, with the measurement. NOTHING WAS REMOVED, DOWNGRADED OR STUBBED.

WHAT 0 MEANS FOR EACH LEVER I TOUCHED OR DELIBERATELY DID NOT, read off the declarations:
  MEM_QUOTA        0 is NOT a sentinel. "Entries each owner block may hold; blocks x quota is the whole
                   store." Capacity is DERIVED from it, so 0 is not a setting of the store, it is the
                   store. REFUSED (< 1).
  MEM_OWNERS       0 is NOT a sentinel. "How many eviction partitions the store is split into; 1 is the
                   single global store." 1 already spells everything 0 could mean. REFUSED (< 1).
  MEM_KEY_DEPTH    0 IS a sentinel -- "0 = the full stack", in the help text -- AND is the shipped
                   default. NOT TOUCHED.
  MEM_REKEY_EVERY  0 IS a sentinel: the declared DISARM (memory/api.py::maintain and ::rekey_period).
                   NOT TOUCHED.
  MEM_PROBE_EVERY  0 IS a sentinel: "Setting this to 0 disarms every retrieval-based rule above; the
                   report must say so" (memory/levers.py::MEMLevers). NOT TOUCHED.
  MEM_BLEND_MAX    0 IS a sentinel: "0 turns retrieval's contribution off", the clean retrieval-off
                   null. NOT TOUCHED.
  MEM_SRC_SHARE    0 IS a sentinel: it selects D3's superseded 'pressure is a signal, not a wall' arm,
                   and memory/api.py::census reports quota_arm='pressure_signal' at src_share == 0.
                   NOT TOUCHED.
  MEM_JUDGE_FRAC   0 IS a sentinel AND the shipped default: "0.0 re-scores nothing". NOT TOUCHED.
  DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX / DATA_EXPOSURE_SKEW
                   0 is NOT a declared sentinel and is NOT refused: it is the finite "flag every plan"
                   setting and the gate FIRES honestly on it (measured above). -inf is likewise not
                   declared, not refused, and honest. nan and +inf are refused, because on those two
                   the gate cannot fire and prints "armed, did not fire" -- a verdict its own
                   arithmetic contradicts.

WHAT THESE REFUSALS DO NOT CLAIM, AND I HAVE NOT WRITTEN OTHERWISE ANYWHERE IN THE TREE. Neither
lever pair is now safe, bounded or validated. The MEM pair is closed BELOW 1 and open above: nothing
declares an upper bound, MEM_QUOTA=10**9 still asks Store.__init__ for 64 billion rows, and
MEM_OWNERS above FAB_SLOTS still folds silently through the same min() I did not touch. The DATA pair
is closed at two values each and open otherwise: DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX=1e26 is finite, passes the check,
and is exactly as uncrossable as +inf while printing as an ordinary number -- which is the same shape
as the ruling's FAB_ALPHA=1e26 cell (aux 0.5150710, composed 2.943258, 15/23 gradient tensors already
non-finite over an ordinary-looking loss pair). A declared per-lever domain is the general answer and
it is the owner's open question; these four refusals do not pre-empt it and do not substitute for it.

NO SWITCH ON EITHER REFUSAL, deliberately. ckpt/api.py::REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD states that a range

refusals and both follow those three. MEM's existing REFUSE_NEGATIVE_PERIOD governs MEM_REKEY_EVERY

findings.detail: CONFIRMED AND CLOSED BELOW 1. Reproduced exactly as the sweep filed it, then refused. BEFORE: MEM_QUOTA=0 assembles with no warning, the d_capacity coupling computes _owner_blocks(FAB.slots, MEM.owners) * int(MEM.quota) = 64 * 0 = 0, and open_store's own `capacity != owners * quota` guard -- which exists to stop 'one quantity, two answers' after E7.40's 24x silent shrink -- PASSES on the identity 0 == 64 * 0, so the whole editable store is allocated with zero rows: keys.shape=(0, 128), counters store.n_opened: 0 beside store.blocks: 64 (sixty-four owner blocks that can hold nothing), and Gate mem.key_depth prints UNREACHABLE (0 vs 0) over it. MEM declares no `enabled` lever, so that is an undeclared off-switch for the mechanism goal B rests on, and Store._block_of is `int(row) // self.quota`. ALSO MEASURED AND NOT IN THE SWEEP: MEM_QUOTA=-5 gives d_capacity=-320 and a bare 'RuntimeError: zeros: Dimension size must be non-negative' out of Store.__init__ naming no lever, and MEM_QUOTA=0.4 truncates to 0 in spine/lever.py::Lever.coerce with build() returning no warning while Config.given() still says '0.4'. AFTER: refused at src/memory/api.py::open_store, first statement of the body, by LeverError naming the generated env name, the RESOLVED integer and the raw string the environment supplied. The test is `< 1`, so it covers 0, every negative and every fractional value that truncates into that range under one clause. 0 is NOT a declared sentinel here -- the help text is 'Entries each owner block may hold; blocks x quota is the whole store' and capacity is derived from it -- so the refusal removes no declared configuration; MEM_QUOTA=1 is a one-entry block and still builds.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED AND CLOSED BELOW 1. WHERE THE REWRITE HAPPENS, established: spine/assemble.py::_owner_blocks, `max(1, min(int(expert_slots), int(owner_buckets)))`, called by BOTH the MEM.d_owner_blocks and MEM.d_capacity coupling rows during spine/assemble.py::build -- i.e. before any Config is frozen and long before MEM sees the value. WHETHER TO REFUSE 0 OR TO REPORT THE REWRITE: REFUSE, and the deciding measurement is that MEM_OWNERS=0, MEM_OWNERS=-5 and MEM_OWNERS=1 open the BYTE-IDENTICAL store (capacity=128, quota=128, owners=1, blocks=1). memory/levers.py::MEMLevers declares owners=1 as 'the single global store', so 1 already spells everything 0 could mean and spells it without a rewrite; reporting the rewrite would keep a configuration that has no meaning of its own and would leave the frozen Config answering mem.owners == 0 beside a store carrying owners=1, which is the printed-number-is-a-lie shape train/api.py::startup_refusals already refuses one package over for RUN_EPOCHS=0. WHY THE FIX IS NOT IN THE SPINE'S FOLD, and this is the part the work list asked to be established: that same max(1, ...) has a SECOND job -- memory/levers.py::MEMLevers declares that 'the d_owner_blocks fold already collapses to 1 block when FAB.slots is 0, so fabric-off degrades correctly with no second knob and no AND'. Deleting the max(1, ...) would take the fabric-off degradation with it. One expression, two jobs, only the lever half wrong -- so the refusal goes on the lever. AND YES, MEM_OWNERS IS READ OUTSIDE THIS PACKAGE: the two coupling rows above are its first reads in the tree, which is why the refusal at src/memory/api.py::open_store is written down as MEM's SECOND line rather than as the first, in the same shape fabric/api.py::manage_period keeps for FAB_MANAGE_EVERY beside the assembly's arithmetic: a refusal that lives only in another package's coupling table disappears when that row is edited, with nothing saying so. open_store's LEVERS READ line was updated in the same edit -- it used to say this package 'never reads it directly', which was true until now.

findings.detail: CONFIRMED AT ALL FOUR CELLS AND CLOSED AT nan AND +inf; 0 AND -inf DELIBERATELY LEFT. I VERIFIED WHAT THE GATE PRINTS AT EACH VALUE BEFORE DECIDING, which is what the work list asked. At nan every comparison `max(vals) > nan` / `skew > nan` is False for every possible exposure; at +inf no finite exposure can exceed the bound. On both, the gate CANNOT fire, and spine/gate.py::Gate receives the default reachable=True, so it renders the middle state: 'armed, did not fire (0.75 vs nan)' and '(3.0 vs inf)'. That is the exact three-state collapse spine/gate.py's own docstring exists to refuse ('reachable=False means the condition CANNOT be met on this configuration, which is not a measurement at all'), and it lands on the two guards ISSUES P3-H22 and Decision D8 are about: data/levers.py::DATALevers says DATA_DRAW defaults to 'planned' because that 'is the only value under which the startup gate is EXACT, and a startup gate is the only thing that can refuse a bad configuration BEFORE it spends the GPU time' -- a bound nothing can cross hands that guarantee straight back, and this time without even the P1-H58 caveat, because the caveat rides on the same `reason` the report still prints. WHY A REFUSAL AND NOT reachable=False: the skew gate ALREADY has a declared unreachable arm at n_areas == 1, and that one is STRUCTURAL (a max/min ratio over one area is undefined; no lever changes it). A threshold nothing can cross is an out-of-range value the operator typed, which this tree refuses by name at the first read; rendering both under one word would put a lever fault and a shape fact in the same sentence. That structural arm still prints 'UNREACHABLE (None vs 3.0)' and is untouched -- measured. WHY 0 AND -inf ARE NOT REFUSED: on both, the gate genuinely FIRES and the printed word is true -- 'FIRED (0.75 vs 0.0)', 'FIRED (0.75 vs -inf)', 'FIRED (3.0 vs 0.0)', 'FIRED (3.0 vs -inf)'. That is the 'flag every plan' configuration, it reports correctly, and refusing it would be the untrippable-guard class inverted. Neither is a DECLARED sentinel and this edit does not mint one for them; the declarations now say so explicitly. SCOPE, STATED IN THE CODE AND NOT ONLY HERE: four cells closed, the class open. DATA_EXPOSURE_MAX=1e26 is finite, passes the check, and is exactly as uncrossable as +inf while printing as an ordinary number. NOT TOUCHED, AND NOT MINE TO TOUCH IN THIS ITEM: DATA_HOLDOUT_FRAC at nan/+/-inf still raises a bare ValueError/OverflowError out of data/api.py::open_areas, which runs BEFORE data_plan -- a second check in data_plan would be an untrippable guard. It is filed in `unfinished`.

MEM_QUOTA=10**9 passes the new refusal and asks Store.__init__ for 64 billion rows; MEM_OWNERS above FAB_SLOTS still folds silently to FAB_SLOTS through the min() in spine/assemble.py::_owner_blocks, which is the same silent-rewrite class as the max(1, ...) A declared per-lever domain is the general answer to both and it is the owner's open question; these refusals do not pre-empt it. Every one of these limits is written into the raised messages themselves, not only here.
